name: IKS Darkkiller
_comment: R3.164, Module R12 'Unusual Ships' SSD book page 25 — NOT R3, which is why this hull sat in
TokenArtClaimedTest's parked list while the rest of the Klingon set was entered. Corner reads
YS:135 DK:7 EX:18 CR:9; annex crew 46, 16 boarding parties, two bonus HETs, point value 120
A D6 command variant, and isLeader like the D5C and D7C (S8.36). Command rating 9 against the
FOUR drone racks of TWO kinds, which is the unusual part: racks 1 and 2 are type-A, racks 3
and 4 are type-E (owner, 2026-10-12 — I had read them as type-F), and the sheet says that
pair 'launch drones at their maximum rate irrespective of the type-A drone racks'. The D6L
refit then replaces them with ADDs outright.
Counted at 600 dpi after the survey cruisers taught the lesson: SCTY is ONE box in the hull
and one in the boom, so security 2 — a 400 dpi crop read it as two in the hull. Transporters
are 7 (one in the boom, two groups of three in the hull), which is high for the chassis and
was counted rather than inherited. Tractors are 2 BEFORE the mech-tractor refit; the two extra
beams are drawn with a black wedge to mark them as refit-only, and the sheet says 'THE
TRACTORS ARE NOT PRESENT WITHOUT THE REFIT'.
SERVICE YEAR DISAGREEMENT, flagged rather than resolved: the SSD corner reads YS:135 and the
Master Annex's ship chart says 136. The sheet is used here. Everything else the two sources
share — crew, boarding parties, BPV, command rating, excess damage — agrees exactly.
_refitComment: Five lines on the ship data table, which is more than any hull entered so far:
D6L REFIT (Y146) = +11, 1 UIM STANDARD FROM Y165, DERFACS FROM Y165 = +5,
The UIM is STANDARD rather than a refit, so it is declared in auxiliary above and the year
logic withholds it before Y165 on its own, exactly as it does for the D7N.
The D6L refit does three things in one, all stated on the sheet: 'THE D6L REFIT CONVERTS THE
THREE FX PHASER-2Ks TO PHASER-1s, CONVERTS THE TYPE-F DRONE RACKS TO ADDs, AND INCREASES THE
RANGE OF THE DISRUPTORS TO 30 HEXES.' The resulting ship is a D6L, following the same naming
the D7C does when ITS refit makes a D7L rather than a D7CK.
Y175 adds the racks' second reload: 'SHIP HAD TYPE-A DRONE RACKS WITH ONE RELOAD UNTIL THE
D6L REFIT WHICH CONVERTED THE DRONE RACKS TO TYPE-B WITH ONE RELOAD. THE Y175 REFIT ADDED A
SECOND RELOAD.' The ADD round count is handled generically — applyYearUpgrades takes every
ADD_6 to ADD_12 at Y175, which is what 'ADDs HAD SIX ROUNDS EACH UNTIL THE Y175 REFIT' says.
The sheet's note that the type-E racks launch at full rate irrespective of the type-A ones is
ALREADY TRUE here, checked 2026-10-12: racks do not constrain one another, and DroneRack
encodes FD3.5 properly — a type-E has four spaces, one reload, fires FOUR times a turn, and
its accepts() takes type-VI dogfight drones and nothing else. So racks 3 and 4 will behave as
the sheet describes without further work; the clause would only need stating if a per-ship
